steps.text: Whisk together the brown sugar, olive oil, soy sauce, lemon pepper, thyme, basil, parsley, and garlic powder in a bowl, and pour into a resealable plastic bag. Add the salmon fillets, coat with the marinade, squeeze out excess air, and seal the bag. Marinate in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour, turning occasionally.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium heat, and lightly oil the grate. Remove the salmon from the marinade, and shake off excess. Discard the remaining marinade.
Grill the salmon on the preheated grill until browned and the fish flakes easily with a fork, about 5 minutes on each side.

raw_recipe.headline: Heather’s Grilled Salmon
raw_recipe.description: A simple marinade of brown sugar and soy sauce is jazzed up with the addition of lemon pepper and some dried herbs. Grilled salmon never tasted so good!

video.description: Grilled salmon is treated to a simple and flavorful marinade.

review.reviewBody: Excellent salmon! I really wanted to make this on the outdoor grill, but we are in the middle of a heat wave right now and it's too hot to do anything outside. So I ended up making this on the George Foreman Grill. I marinated the salmon for about 3 hours and the salmon was so tender and flavorful. I set some of the marinade aside and simmered it on the stove for a few minutes then spooned it over top the finished salmon. Delicious! Can't wait to try this on the outdoor grill.

I made the marinade as described but did not have parsley. It didn't seem to miss it but next time I'll make sure I do. Using a baking dish, I sprinkled a little sea salt on the salmon before adding the marinade and then a few sprinkles of Old Bay blackened seasoning just for good measure. Placed the salmon in the refrigerator for only a hour and flipped it a few times while spooning the good stuff on top. Next time I'll plan ahead and make sure it sits a little longer. While my husband put them on the grill, I look the leftover marinade and heated it on the stove. We used lightly oiled foil to make for easy clean up. Five minutes, flipped and continued cooking another six. It was amazing and not only will this be a staple in our home but I think it's going to be a great meal for company. Thanks again, Allrecipes saved the day once again!

Heather has presented a great combination of flavors to elevate this delicious fish. Not having lemon pepper, I squeezed fresh lemon juice into the marinade and cracked pepper. Also, being January, I used the Ninja Foodi and air crisp feature for 12 minutes at 390 degrees. Absolutely perfect Salmon. If you don't like that crispy skin, it comes right off after air crisping. Leave it on while crisping, though, as it helps keep the Salmon moist and delicious.
marinaded 4 hours, then 280 in smoker for 45 minutes - drop down delicious!

Excellent recipe!! I used skiless salmon steaks and followed the recipe for marinating. I didn't have basil but added oregano. I marinated for a little longer approximately 2 hours. Cook time was about 1 1\2 hours on my pellet grill set to 225 degrees. I used traditional charcoal wood blend pellets. I didn't flip the steaks and they turned out great very flavorful and moist. Thanks for the recipe Heather.

I use the marinade on everything. My fav is actually on bone in chicken thighs with carrots , mushrooms, onions, and whatever you want to add and cook in slow cooker. It cooks in less than 2 hours. I brown chicken, and double sauce. Serve over rice.

Perfect, a family favorite! I've been making this for 5 years now, none of us can even order salmon at a restaurant because it's always a letdown after this. I also bake it in the oven, when doing so I bake at 400 for 20-25 minutes depending on the thickness and I bake it in the marinade it comes out so tender! Sometimes I use hoisin sauce in place of brown sugar/olive oil combo. Also I use half the sugar and it's still delicious!

This was absolutely AWESOME! I added a teaspoon of ground ginger to give it a bit of a "tang". I also broiled on high for 10 minutes. Tender, sweet (but not too sweet), tingle of ginger...this was great. I'm doing this every time!

Excellent flavor & easy too make. I smoked them on my Traeger for an hour @ 225. Removed them and raised the temperature to 375. Placed them back on the grill for three minutes on each side. The came out perfct!
I subbed Splenda brown sugar for diabetic reasons. Great tasting marinade.

I had bought some fresh grouper and wanted something extra to add to it before I placed it on the grill. I used this sauce and the flavor was amazing. The only change I made was using Splenda brown sugar, my husband has to watch his blood sugar. It came out so flavorful. I did what another review suggested and kept some of the marinade and heated it to use as an additional sauce after the fish was grilled. AMAZING, I will use this recipe again

Delicious! I was so confident about this recipe being top-notch that I made it for guests without testing it first. I followed the recipe with just 2 modifications - I left out the thyme (no “thyme” to go to the grocery store to pick some up.). And, we smoked it on the pellet smoker for about 55 minutes on super-smoke and then increased the heat to 300, until it reached the internal temperature of 145 degrees. I made an extra half recipe of the sauce, warmed it up in the microwave to use as extra sauce. It was a huge hit! This is definitely a keeper!

Great tasting Salmon. I sear meat side then flip and grill on skin side down. The skin usually sticks and peels off rather than getting crispy, even if I grease the grill. I cook the thinnest par of the filet on a piece of foil to keep from burning.

I used my own homemade marinade for this recipe and it turned out fantastic! The flavors soaked in perfectly and the salmon was juicy and delicious. Highly recommend trying it with your favorite marinade.
This is my favorite way to make salmon- even beats fancy restaurants dishes, imo.
I baked it in the oven for 20 minutes. My family complained I did not have enough. This is a great recipe. Thank you.
